html:
The map's label for the many states of the Irrawaddy valley in what is now Myanmar, from 1492 to 1600. After the empire of Pagan broke up in the late 1200s, no single power held the whole country for some 250 years.

The main players were:

  • the Ava Kingdom in the dry zone of Upper Burma;
  • Hanthawaddy, the Mon kingdom of the south, rich from sea trade through Pegu;
  • the Shan states in the hills to the north and east;
  • Arakan on the western coast;
  • the small kingdom of Toungoo.

Toungoo changed everything. Its king Tabinshwehti united most of the valley in the 1530s and 1540s, and his successor Bayinnaung conquered the Shan states, Lan Na and Ayutthaya, building one of the largest empires in Southeast Asian history. It fell apart soon after his death in 1581, but the Taungoo and Konbaung kings rebuilt a united Burma in the 1600s.
